resolutions: An honorific begins with a complete owner-issued neutral VNC Source rather than a copied formula or surface spelling.
Typed Source analysis records whether causative, applicative, or both productive honorific formations are licensed.
A sole licensed formation is automatic, while two licensed formations create one genuine user choice.
The respected participant is a user choice only where the typed participant structure leaves a genuine ambiguity.
Self-honorification is tested against the actually respected participant rather than against first-person form alone.
A first-person subject may honor an existing object but cannot select an absent object as the respected participant.
The honorific reflexive relation and its coreference with the Result subject are automatic.
English H notation and translations remain reading evidence and never authorize grammar.
A causative honorific reuses the canonical causative derivation owner.
An applicative honorific reuses the canonical applicative derivation owner.
Monomorphemic and polymorphemic unlisted typed Sources receive the same productive honorific treatment.
Morphemic Source structure preserves exact boundaries, vowel quantity, final shape, class, and valence through honorific derivation.
Canonical causative or applicative shape alternatives are exposed only when more than one owner-licensed Result survives.
A single canonical shape alternative is applied automatically.
Documented irregular, suppletive, connective-preferred, and mood-defective realizations remain lexical facts rather than productive route gates.
A documented example identity cannot authorize or block a productive honorific route by itself.
Typed lexical analysis must match the current Source stem before it can constrain route availability.
Requesting a formation absent from the matching typed Source analysis is blocked.
Causative honorifics preserve the autonomous-agent interpretation and add reflexive causee structure automatically.
Applicative honorifics preserve the acting-in-one's-own-interest interpretation and add a reflexive beneficiary automatically.
An honorific-only applicative remains a typed lexical fact and does not become a general applicative restriction.
A preferred causative or applicative route is guidance when both remain licensed and never silently removes the other route.
The huica-tz optative restriction follows its lexical formation analysis before an invalid finite base can obscure it.
Every accepted writing atom observes an owner-issued canonical Result and an exact clickable cue.
Every accepted reading atom observes one exact collapsed Lesson 33 reading idea.
Removing any accepted atom from its writing cue or reading idea removes exact implementation credit for that atom.
A projective applicative honorific preserves every owner-issued projective object before adding its reflexive beneficiary.
Projective object person, number, governor, and grammatical role remain properties of the captured Source rather than new honorific controls.
The reflexive applicative beneficiary is added automatically and remains coreferential with the Result subject.
Third-person projective Sources preserve the genuine ambiguity between honoring the subject and honoring an existing object.
A first-person projective subject cannot honor itself, so the existing object becomes the honored participant automatically.
English H placement cannot select the honored participant or rewrite the Nahuatl participant topology.
Neutral and honorific examples check the productive rule but do not authorize a projective Source stem.
A causative or applicative VNC may enter the derived-Source honorific route only as its complete owner-issued Result.
The inner derivation, higher agent, lower agent or source participant, themes, inherited objects, and morphemic boundaries remain part of the captured Source.
A first-person embedded participant is excluded from the respected-object candidates while an eligible nonspecific theme remains available.
A retained nonspecific theme permits singular or plural contextual reference without a separate number control.
Retyped stems, reconstructed formulas, copied surfaces, and Canvas examples cannot replace the owner-issued derived Source.
Causative, applicative, and unlisted typed Source shapes receive the same derived-Source continuation when their canonical participant topology matches.
A projective causative honorific retains the owner-issued patient and adds a subject-coreferential reflexive agent; it does not replace the patient with a reflexive object.
Agent-versus-patient honorific ambiguity is exposed only when both readings survive the typed participant facts; a sole reading is automatic.
Causative-only, applicative-only, and both-available routes come from typed honorific-formation analysis, never from example-stem membership.
Licensed alternate causative realizations remain a genuine realization choice and do not become competing lexical routes.
First-person projective subjects receive the required nonfirst-person projective object automatically without creating an extra user choice.
Unlisted projective Sources with matching shape and participant facts receive the same honorific derivation, while changed route facts can reject the route without changing the stem.
Mainline-reflexive object topology selects honorific preterit embed automatically; the route is not an additional user choice.
The preterit embed consumes the canonical class-specific perfective and a silent preterit morph rather than asking the user to construct either one.
The complete reflexive preterit predicate replaces the fixed matrix specific object while preserving the Source object pronouns and participants.
The fixed tla-(tzin-o-ā) matrix remains distinct from the embedded Source and is not exposed as a matrix picker.
Shuntline reflexives remain distinct from mainline reflexives and cannot enter the preterit-embed route merely because both have reflexive meaning.
Class A, B, C, and D perfectives are supplied productively by the canonical Source owner; the four Canvas examples do not create a verb list.
Copied formulas, surfaces, example spellings, and manual bracketing cannot replace an owner-issued mainline-reflexive Source Result.
A reverential is a doubled honorific and can begin only from an owner-issued honorific Result, not from a raw or copied honorific-looking stem.
The neutral Source, inner honorific, and outer reverential remain three distinct typed layers with their boundaries preserved.
The second layer inherits the inner honored participant and any genuine subject-object ambiguity; it cannot introduce a new participant selection.
The honorific perfective plus silent preterit predicate becomes the incorporated object of a second fixed tla-(tzin-o-ā) matrix automatically.
Projective objects, reflexive structure, agreement, and participant roles remain continuous through the reverential layer.
Copied honorific spellings, formulas, surfaces, and Canvas examples have no reverential Source authority.
Intransitive, projective-object, and reflexive-object Sources enter one shared pejorative preterit-embed rule when their typed topology is compatible.
The embedded pejorative predicate consumes the canonical perfective supplied productively by the Source verb class.
Silent preterit 0 occupies the replaced matrix-object position and has no surface realization.
Fixed tla-(pōl-o-ā) is automatic, retains the long vowel of affective (-pōl)-Ø-, and is restricted to this pejorative construction.
The complete embedded predicate replaces the matrix specific object without deleting any object pronoun inherited from the Source.
Inherited object person, number, governor, and grammatical role remain typed Source facts rather than new pejorative controls.
First-person subject disparagement and reflexive self-disparagement are allowed; the self-honorification restriction does not transfer to pejoratives.
A projective Source exposes subject-versus-object disparagement only while both participant readings genuinely survive.
A reflexive Source does not manufacture a subject-object choice because its two grammatical roles share one referent.
Class A, B, C, and D examples prove productive perfective behavior and never form a pejorative verbstem whitelist.
Copied formulas, surfaces, example spellings, and caller-supplied bracketing cannot authorize the pejorative route.
Compound honorific and pejorative scope is derived from the complete owner-issued compound Source rather than from a copied spelling.
An ordinary compositional compound with an intransitive matrix transforms its embed.
A compound typed as one lexicalized verbstem transforms its matrix.
A shared-object compound transforms its matrix and retains the shared object in the completed Result.
Compositional versus lexicalized structure is a Source-analysis choice only when both structures genuinely remain available.
The user never receives an independent embed-versus-matrix attitude-scope switch.
The same cui plus huetzi members receive different scope only when their typed compound structure differs.
The connective and both compound members remain part of the canonical Result after attitude transformation.
Owner-issued object carriers, person, number, and participant relations survive compound attitude transformation.
Outer subject, mood, and tense remain outside the transformed compound and are preserved automatically.
Internal morphemic boundaries remain visible across the selected member transformation and completed compound.
Typed lexicalization analysis must match both current Source members before it can affect scope.
Canvas examples, formulas, surfaces, and direct caller scope requests never authorize compound attitude scope.
